entries.name: Reverse Flyes
entries.reason: Source-bound draft, drawn from a 3D model turned 40 degrees so both arms and the bench show. Chest down on a bench inclined at 45 degrees with the feet on the floor; the arms start hanging square to the bench and sweep out and apart in one arc, with one slight fixed elbow bend, until the upper arms are parallel to the floor, hold, and lower more slowly. The chest stays on the bench. Not drawn: the bench angle is not given by the source, so 45 degrees is a drawing choice; the shoulder blades squeezing together, which this figure has no way to show.
entries.summary: Chest down on an incline bench, sweep the dumbbells out and apart with a slight elbow bend until the arms are parallel to the floor, squeeze the shoulder blades, then lower under control.

frames.caption: Lie chest-down on an incline bench with a dumbbell in each hand, palms facing each other, arms hanging perpendicular to the bench.
Holding a slight bend at the elbows, move the weights out and away from each other in an arc until the arms are parallel to the floor.
Keep the chest on the bench.

entries.name: Dumbbell Lying Rear Lateral Raise
entries.reason: Source-bound draft, drawn from a 3D model turned 40 degrees so the shallow 15-degree prone incline bench under the chest, the neutral-grip dumbbells with palms facing each other, and the wide lateral arc of both arms out to shoulder height all read clearly: lying face down on a 15-degree incline bench with arms hanging down and a slight fixed elbow bend, raising the dumbbells out to the sides to shoulder height, holding for one second at the top, and lowering under control.
entries.summary: Lying face down on a shallow 15-degree incline bench holding dumbbells with palms facing each other and a slight elbow bend, raise the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc to shoulder height, hold for one second, and lower under control.

frames.caption: Set an adjustable bench to a shallow 15-degree incline and lie face down with your chest supported, holding a dumbbell in each hand with palms facing each other and arms hanging down.
Maintaining a slight bend in your elbows, raise the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until your arms are at shoulder height.
Hold the contracted position at the top for a second, squeezing your rear delts.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back toward the starting position under control.
Return the dumbbells to the hanging start with your chest glued to the pad and a slight fixed bend in your elbows.

entries.name: Lying Rear Delt Raise
entries.reason: Source-bound draft, drawn from a 3D model turned 40 degrees so the horizontal flat bench supporting the chest, the dumbbells held below the chest with palms facing each other, and the wide lateral arc up to parallel with the floor all read clearly and distinguish the flat bench from the 15-degree incline variant: lying face down on a flat bench, raising the dumbbells out to the sides to shoulder height with a slight fixed elbow bend, holding for one second at the top, and lowering under control.
entries.summary: Lying face down on a flat bench holding dumbbells below your chest with palms facing each other and a slight elbow bend, raise the dumbbells out to the sides until your arms are parallel to the floor at shoulder height, hold for one second, and lower under control.

frames.caption: Lie face down on a flat bench holding a dumbbell in each hand below your chest with palms facing each other and a slight bend in your elbows.
Raise the dumbbells out to the sides in a wide arc until your arms are parallel to the floor at shoulder height.
Hold the top position for a second, squeezing your rear deltoids.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back toward the starting position under control.
Return to the starting position below the chest with your chest flat against the bench and a slight fixed elbow bend.
